charter:
# Charter — T1 Plan spine (retrospective, 2026-11-26)

- **Project:** T1 'Plan spine', track v2, ADM phase G, plateau capability, tranche 1, issue #72 (CLOSED). The build is the delivery commit `e3d7c4eb` (2026-11-17), subject 'plan spine: T1 — the rows, the actions and the ten scenarios (#72) (#250)'. The project row `01a1d039-0d32-7c81-8365-371217d16ef7` carries `status: closed`, `meta.expected_outputs: [project-brief, evidence]`, `meta.closure_outputs: [closure-review]` and `meta.viability: rework`; it was reopened for the #526 retrospective rework under delegation `01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14`.
- **Mandate:** give the conveyor a project plan it can be held to — a promise frozen in an approved baseline, a change path carrying an impact block and the baseline it changes, priority computed from four typed inputs, a portfolio that lists the in-flight set, a dependency graph that refuses a cycle, and MSP programme-definition rows that make a benefit a measurement record and a tranche review an evidence-bearing gate. The same build widens the one gate primitive so a requester or executor can no longer decide the gate judging their own work.
- **Scope:** the T1 row of `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §12, with §8.2, §8.3 and §10.3; `migrations/0044_plan_spine.sql` — `wbs_node`, `project_baseline`, `project_register_item`, `project_dependency`, `programme_cadence`, `programme_tranche`, `benefit_profile`, `benefit_link`, `benefit_transition`, `stakeholder_profile`, `programme_baseline`, the widened `governed_asset` kinds and the programme `shared_config`; the `wbs.*`, `baselines.*`, `registers.*`, `project_dependencies.*`, `portfolio.in_flight`, `cadences.*`, `tranches.*`, `benefits.*` and `stakeholders.profile_*` action families; the requester/executor exclusion in `approvals.decide`; the project-type selection of phase template, gate set and job family; and the DoD gate on `card_type.definition`. Out of scope: the decision ladder (T2), the PM job (T3), cadence materialisation, PI planning and the benefits-realization procedure (T10), metrics (T11), and any migration or retirement of V1's `outline` tree.
- **Expected outputs:** `project-brief`, `evidence`. **Closure outputs:** `closure-review`. **Acceptance instrument:** `acceptance/programme/T1.toml`.
- **Date:** this charter is retrospective and was authored on 2026-11-26. It records the lifecycle of a build completed on 2026-11-17; it does not attest contemporaneous intent and it does not authorise new work beyond the rework.

soaw.title: Statement of Architecture Work — T1 Plan spine (retrospective, 2026-11-26)

body.assignment: Rework the V2 slice T1 (SPEC_V2 §12, issue #72) by the reconstituted TOGAF/MSP lifecycle: author the charter, this Statement of Architecture Work, the seven mandatory Phase A–D artefacts, the delivery contract and the WBS deliverable, record the Phase-G compliance review, re-publish the project-brief and evidence outputs, and re-close through the one gate. The architecture work is the plan spine itself — the rows, the action families, the refusals and the requester exclusion recorded retrospectively and dated 2026-11-26.
body.scope: In scope: `wbs_node` (a phase, deliverable, work-package and milestone tree with the four WSJF inputs and no stored score), `project_baseline` (an append-only frozen snapshot), `project_register_item` (the one six-kind register; a change carries `baseline_ref` and `meta.impact`), `project_dependency` (blocks, needs, supersedes, informs; cycles refused in the creating transaction), the programme `shared_config` inherited by its projects, `programme_cadence`, `programme_tranche`, `benefit_profile`, `benefit_link` (five levels), `benefit_transition`, `stakeholder_profile`, `programme_baseline`, the widened `governed_asset` kinds, the project-type selection of phase template and gate set, and the DoD gate. Out of scope: T2's decision ladder, T3's PM job, T10's cadence materialisation, PI planning and benefits-realization procedure, T11's metrics, and any change to V1's outline tree.
body.responsibilities: The programme architect authors the pack under the #526 rework delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14; the Architecture Board reviews the seven A–D artefacts and both contracts; the programme owner signs the closure. The delivery contract is approved by an approver distinct from the requester, which is the same exclusion the build installs in `approvals.decide`: a requester cannot decide the gate judging their own work. The rework remains retrospective and states its evidence rather than claiming a contemporaneous review.
body.acceptance_criteria: The SPEC_V2 §12 T1 gate: one project with a baseline, a change request and a refused self-approval; WSJF recomputes from inputs; the portfolio view lists the in-flight set; a dependency cycle is refused; a benefit profile without baseline, target, method or owner is refused; a benefit-map edge names its five levels. The ten issue-#72 scenarios are proved by named real-Postgres tests in `crates/actions/tests/plan_spine.rs`, `crates/api/tests/approval_dual.rs` and `crates/actions/tests/programme_baseline.rs`; the rework's acceptance instrument is `acceptance/programme/T1.toml`, and the closure gate is decided by an approver other than its requester.

# Stakeholder map — T1 plan spine

## Metadata

Retrospective matrix for T1, authored 2026-11-26 from `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §12, `migrations/0044_plan_spine.sql` and the rework transcript. Phase a, plateau psa, kind matrix; owner the programme architect under the #526 rework delegation; reviewer the Architecture Board; project 01a1d039-0d32-7c81-8365-371217d16ef7; subject the plan spine and the MSP rows around it.

## Entries

Seven actors. The sponsoring group decides the tranche authorisation and the exit criteria that consume the capability. The SRO is accountable for the coherent capability and its benefits. The benefit owner holds each benefit's baseline, target, method and transition. The PM job consumes the WBS, baseline and change control rows. The Architecture Board approves the A–D set and the two contracts. The delivery teams accept the WBS rows and live under the dependency edges. Operators and tenants supply the tenant configuration that defines the in-flight set.

## Links

This artefact carries one typed edge: Requirements catalog — T1 plan spine as dependency, because the requirements fix what each actor receives from the rows and their refusals. Every edge names another artefact this pack creates, so the set has no orphan.

## Document

Purpose: place the actors of the plan spine so each concern has a named owner and a stated engagement. Scope: the stakeholders of the capability delivered by issue #72 and of the tranche-1 governance around it. It was reconstructed retrospectively on 2026-11-26 from the recorded roles rather than from a live elicitation, and it does not claim that any actor re-accepted the records after the 2026-11-17 close.

# Driver/goal/objective — T1 plan spine

## Metadata

Retrospective catalogue for T1, authored 2026-11-26 from the slice record, the migration and the transcript. Phase a, plateau psa, kind catalog; owner the programme architect under the #526 rework delegation; reviewer the Architecture Board; project 01a1d039-0d32-7c81-8365-371217d16ef7; subject the drivers behind the plan spine and the objective each row installs.

## Entries

Eight drivers, each with a goal and a measurable objective. D1 records the unfrozen promise; G1 makes the baseline immutable. D2 records the silent edit; G2 requires an impact block and a baseline reference. D3 records self-approval; G3 installs dual control in the one gate primitive. D4 records opinion-driven priority; G4 computes WSJF on read from four typed inputs. D5 records the missing portfolio; G5 makes the in-flight set a tenant-configured read. D6 records a JSON dependency list; G6 refuses cycles in the creating transaction. D7 records prose benefits and evidence-free reviews; G7 makes both measurement records. D8 records an untyped project and an unenforced done condition; G8 selects the template and gate set from the project type and gates on the card type's DoD.

## Links

This artefact carries one typed edge: Stakeholder map — T1 plan spine as derivation, because each driver is held by an actor named there. Every edge names another artefact this pack creates, so the set has no orphan.

## Document

Purpose: trace why the plan spine exists and what each row is meant to achieve. Scope: baseline and change control, dual control, prioritisation, the portfolio read, dependency edges, the MSP rows, project typing and the DoD gate. It was authored retrospectively on 2026-11-26 from the verified tests and the migration, and it records the objective the specification set rather than claiming that a later reader can reproduce the 2026-11-17 build.

Twelve requirements. R1 to R3 fix the frozen baseline, the impact-bearing change and the refused self-approval. R4 makes WSJF a read computation over four stored inputs. R12 ties the project type to the phase template, gate set and job family, and places the DoD on the card type so the domain layer can enforce it.

## Links

## Document

# Solution concept — T1 plan spine

## Metadata

Retrospective diagram for T1, authored 2026-11-26 from `migrations/0044_plan_spine.sql`, the action families and the transcript. Phase a, plateau psa, kind diagram; owner the programme architect under the #526 rework delegation; reviewer the Architecture Board; project 01a1d039-0d32-7c81-8365-371217d16ef7; subject the rows and edges that carry the plan spine.

## Entries

Twenty-two rows: fifteen components and seven edges. The tree, the frozen baseline, the six-kind register, the directed dependency graph, the programme shared configuration, the cadence and tranche rows, the benefit profile, link and transition records, the stakeholder profile, the programme baseline and the widened governed-asset kinds are the storage. approvals.decide is the one gate primitive and portfolio.in_flight is a computed read. The edges record what freezes what, what a change must point at, where the dependency source lives, how WSJF is read without a stored score, how a benefit map names its profile, and what a tranche review needs before it can decide.

## Links

This artefact carries one typed edge: Requirements catalog — T1 plan spine as realization, because the components and edges exist to satisfy those twelve requirements. Every edge names another artefact this pack creates, so the set has no orphan.

## Document

Purpose: show the components and edges that turn a specification row into a plan a project can be held to. Scope: the migration's rows, the programme shared configuration, the spine action families and the requester-aware gate. It was drawn retrospectively on 2026-11-26 from the delivered schema and the recorded build order, not from a design session held before the work.

# Business capability map — T1 plan spine

Twelve capabilities, nine live and three stated as partial or owned elsewhere. Baseline and change control, dual control, WSJF, the in-flight portfolio, the dependency graph, the programme-definition rows, the benefit measurement record and the tranche gate are live and proved. Project typing and the DoD gate are live through project_type_code and card_type.definition. Cadence materialisation and PI planning are T10. The console is partial: only portfolio.in_flight is live, while the Plan tab's screens remain T1 work and the other tabs are fixtures.

It is retrospective and dated 2026-11-26; it records the capabilities as delivered at the 2026-11-17 build and does not upgrade a partial capability into a live one.

# Technology standards — T1 plan spine

## Metadata

Retrospective catalogue for T1, authored 2026-11-26 from the migration and the delivery record. Phase d, plateau hld, kind catalog; owner the programme architect under the #526 rework delegation; reviewer the Architecture Board; project 01a1d039-0d32-7c81-8365-371217d16ef7; subject the standards the plan spine fixes for every later slice.

## Entries

Twelve standards. PostgreSQL 18 carries forced row-level security on every new table and the migration stays forward-only. The workspace is edition 2024 with unsafe code forbidden, and the tests are real-Postgres integration tests. One ActionSpec serves HTTP, MCP and the served spec over unversioned routes with RFC 9457 errors. WSJF is arithmetic on read from four typed inputs, and the cycle check is a reachability query inside the creating transaction. Optimistic concurrency and a fixed error vocabulary make refusals stable. Verification runs on real Postgres and then the GitHub-hosted preflight. The programme's shared configuration is inherited rather than restated, and the Definition of Done is data on the card type that the domain layer enforces.

## Links

This artefact carries one typed edge: Data entity catalog — T1 plan spine as derivation, because each entity is held in one of these formats or enforced by one of these disciplines. Every edge names another artefact this pack creates, so the set has no orphan.

## Document

Purpose: name the formats, disciplines and instruments the plan spine fixes, and where each one is enforced. Scope: Postgres and row-level security, the migration set, the action registry, WSJF arithmetic, the cycle check, the error vocabulary, verification, shared configuration and the DoD. It was authored retrospectively on 2026-11-26 and names only standards that the delivered migration, the tests and the delivery plan actually apply.

# Architecture Artefact Index — T1 (retrospective, 2026-11-26)

## Metadata

The artefact set for T1 is the seven mandatory Phase A–D artefacts on the delivery track (track v2): the Stakeholder map, the Driver/goal/objective, the Requirements catalog and the Solution concept at phase a, plateau psa, and the Business capability map, the Data entity catalog and the Technology standards at phases b, c and d, plateau hld. Each is an approved row with a published body; the owner is the programme architect under the #526 rework delegation, the reviewer is the Architecture Board, and the subject is project 01a1d039-0d32-7c81-8365-371217d16ef7, the plan spine.

## Entries

The set is seven rows in the order the standard seeds them: Stakeholder map — T1 plan spine (matrix), Driver/goal/objective — T1 plan spine (catalog), Requirements catalog — T1 plan spine (catalog), Solution concept — T1 plan spine (diagram), Business capability map — T1 plan spine (diagram), Data entity catalog — T1 plan spine (catalog) and Technology standards — T1 plan spine (catalog). Each carries its own entries: seven stakeholders, eight drivers, twelve requirements, twenty-two components and edges, twelve capabilities, sixteen entities and twelve standards.

## Links

The typed edges are: the driver catalogue derives from the stakeholder map; the requirements catalogue derives from the driver catalogue; the solution concept realizes the requirements catalogue; the capability map derives from the solution concept and the requirements catalogue; the data entity catalogue derives from the capability map and the solution concept; and the technology standards derive from the data entity catalogue. Every edge names another artefact of this pack, so no artefact is an orphan.

## Document

The index is the architecture-artifact page the artefact standard reads. The seven artefact rows bind to the adopted standard keys stakeholder_map, driver_goal_objective, requirements_catalog, solution_concept, business_capability_map, data_entity_catalog and technology_standards, and this index is the retrospective page authored on 2026-11-26 over them. It records the set the rework produces; it does not claim that a contemporaneous artefact existed at the 2026-11-17 close.

risk.title: A later consumer reads a cadence row as a working PI rhythm
risk.body: T1 stores programme_cadence rows but T10 owns materialising their cards, PI planning and the benefits-realization procedure. A reader who sees the row without that boundary may treat the rhythm as delivered. This retrospective row, dated 2026-11-26, keeps the boundary live: the row is the storage T10 consumes, and the Portfolio page's cadence and capacity tabs remain fixtures until T10 lands.

meta.owner: the programme architect under the #526 rework delegation

requirements: docs/SPEC_V2.md §12 — T1 cadence and MSP rows

risk.title: An edit after a baseline is expected to appear in the frozen scope
risk.body: project_baseline is append-only and a take freezes the WBS and register facts as they were. A project member who edits a WBS row after the take and then reads the baseline will not see the edit, which is the intended behaviour but an easy surprise. The P1.1 test proves the snapshot does not move; this row records the operational risk that a reader misreads the frozen copy as a stale bug and edits around it.

meta.owner: the programme architect under the #526 rework delegation

risk.title: The in-flight set is tenant configuration, so a misconfiguration hides live work
risk.body: portfolio.in_flight is a computed read over the tenant's configured status set, default active and paused. A tenant that narrows or mistypes that configuration will silently drop work from the portfolio without any row changing. The read model is correct by construction, but its input is configuration; this row records the risk that the portfolio is trusted as a complete inventory when it is only complete for the configured set.

meta.owner: the programme architect under the #526 rework delegation

issue.title: No contemporaneous governance record existed at the 2026-11-17 close
issue.body: No charter, Statement of Architecture Work, delivery contract, Phase-G review or closure review was authored before T1 closed on 2026-11-17. The records in this rework are retrospective and dated 2026-11-26; they reconstitute the lifecycle from the delivered commit, the migration, the named tests and the published inception and architecture outputs. The issue stays open as a fact about the record rather than as a defect the pack can close.

issue.title: The Plan tab's WBS, baseline and register screens are not a console delivery
issue.body: The plan spine is an action and data capability. The Portfolio page's WSJF-backlog, cadence and capacity tabs remain fixtures, and the Plan tab's WBS, baseline and register screens are T1 work recorded here rather than a delivered console. Only portfolio.in_flight is live. This issue records the gap between the served capability and the rendered console so a later UI slice claims the screens explicitly.

assumption.title: Every gate passes through approvals.decide, so the requester exclusion covers the whole programme
assumption.body: The requester and executor exclusion is installed in one primitive, approvals.decide, and applies to every action approval rather than only T1's. That is only as strong as the assumption that no gate bypasses the primitive and writes an approval_decision row directly. The P1.3 test proves the exclusion where it runs; this retrospective assumption, recorded 2026-11-26, states the condition under which the exclusion is programme-wide.

assumption.title: The four WSJF inputs are valid integers for every WBS row that reaches the read
assumption.body: WSJF divides the sum of three non-negative integers by job_size, and the column constraints require job_size > 0. The computation therefore assumes that no row reaches the read with a null input or a zero size, including rows written before the constraint or through a path that skips validation. This row records the assumption on 2026-11-26; the arithmetic has no defensive branch for an invalid row, by design.

dependency.title: T2, T3, T9 and T10 build on the plan-spine rows
dependency.body: SPEC_V2 §12 records T0 to T1 to T2 to T3, with T9 and T10 after T1 and T3. The decision ladder, the PM job, the ADM capability and the SAFe cadence all read the WBS, baseline, register, dependency, tranche and benefit rows this slice creates. The dependency runs one way: a change to a row's shape or refusal after T1 is a change to every consumer's contract, not a local edit.

dependency.title: The frozen baseline depends on the take and the snapshot sharing one transaction
dependency.body: The P1.1 test proves a later row edit cannot move the baseline because the take writes the snapshot inside the same transaction that reads the rows. The dependency is on that transaction boundary holding for every baseline kind, scope, schedule and cost alike. This retrospective row records the dependency on 2026-11-26 and notes that it is an invariant of the store path rather than a property of the reader.

benefit.title: Priority is arithmetic and never a stale stored score
benefit.body: WSJF is computed on read from four typed inputs, so a change to business value, time criticality, risk reduction or job size moves the score with the edit and no backfill is possible or needed. The benefit is that a backlog order cannot drift from the inputs it claims, which the P2.1 test demonstrates by moving the read score after an input edit. Recorded retrospectively on 2026-11-26.

benefit.title: A tranche review cannot decide without baselines, benefit status and the risk register
benefit.body: tranches.review refuses 422 tranche_evidence_missing unless the three evidence sets are present, and with them records continue, pause or stop and moves the tranche state. The benefit is that a tranche decision is an evidence-bearing gate rather than a meeting note: the review cannot be convened on narrative alone. Recorded retrospectively on 2026-11-26.

benefit.title: Self-approval is refused on every gate, not only where a test looks
benefit.body: The exclusion lives in approvals.decide, the one primitive every gate uses, and compares the pending row's requester and executor with the actor before any approval_decision row is written. The benefit is that the refusal is structural: a new gate inherits it without adding a check. The requester test in approval_dual.rs and the taker test in programme_baseline.rs prove the two entry points recorded here on 2026-11-26.

body.commitments: Deliver the plan spine of SPEC_V2 §12: `wbs_node`, `project_baseline`, `project_register_item`, `project_dependency`, the programme `shared_config` and cadence, `programme_tranche`, `benefit_profile`, `benefit_link`, `benefit_transition`, `stakeholder_profile`, `programme_baseline` and the widened `governed_asset` kinds, with the project-type selection of phase template and gate set, the DoD gate on `card_type.definition`, and the requester and executor exclusion in `approvals.decide`. The build is one WBS deliverable accepted with WSJF inputs business value 8, time criticality 5, risk reduction 8 and job size 8.
body.compliance: T1 is assessed clause by clause against the SPEC_V2 §12 gate and the ten issue-#72 scenarios. Each scenario has one named real-Postgres test in `crates/actions/tests/plan_spine.rs`, `crates/api/tests/approval_dual.rs` or `crates/actions/tests/programme_baseline.rs`, and the refusal slugs are stable: 409 dependency_cycle, 409 self_approval, 422 change_impact_missing, 422 benefit_profile_incomplete, 422 benefit_map_incomplete, 422 tranche_evidence_missing and 422 self_dependency. The Phase-G review 01a1ff8b-b3ac-7082-bc16-df2f97bd7f8d records the level compliant against this contract, and the rework's acceptance instrument is `acceptance/programme/T1.toml`.
body.approval: The delivery contract 01a1ff8a-754f-70de-a63a-fa8d00596433 is approved under approval 01a1ff8a-880f-7d08-b322-9656f2c5355f by an approver distinct from the requester, which is the same exclusion the build installs in the gate primitive. The Statement of Architecture Work 01a1ff89-02bd-7b6d-902e-ffa5902cc7f5 sits under its own approval 01a1ff89-1794-79d0-8707-f7614987ee7c, and the scope baseline 01a1ff8a-b4f0-7e6e-9cc7-4231076e1039 (kind scope, taken 2026-11-21) was approved by the same approver. The Phase-G review 01a1ff8b-b3ac-7082-bc16-df2f97bd7f8d cites this contract.
body.acceptance: Acceptance is executable. The ten scenarios run against real Postgres 18: a baseline that does not move, a change refused without an impact block or baseline, a refused self-approval, WSJF recomputed from inputs with no stored column, the in-flight portfolio, a refused two-node cycle and a refused deep cycle with no partial row, a refused benefit profile missing baseline, target, method or owner, a benefit-map edge naming its five levels, and a tranche review refused without baselines, benefit status and the risk register. The manifest `acceptance/programme/T1.toml` is the rework's acceptance instrument.
body.evidence: The evidence route is the delivery commit `e3d7c4eb` (2026-11-17), issue #72 CLOSED, `migrations/0044_plan_spine.sql`, the named test functions, the published inception analysis and architecture design of 2026-11-16, the seven Phase A–D artefacts, the scope baseline 01a1ff8a-b4f0-7e6e-9cc7-4231076e1039, the Phase-G review 01a1ff8b-b3ac-7082-bc16-df2f97bd7f8d and the rework record in `docs/evidence/rework/T1.json` and `docs/evidence/rework/tranche-1/acts.md`. The published outputs are the project brief and the evidence page.

values.approval_policy_defaults: one approver; the requester and the executor are excluded by approvals.decide on every gate
values.budget: the tranche-1 budget line recorded on the programme row
values.cadence: pi, sprint, demo, retro and refinement rows in programme_cadence; T10 materialises their cards

wbs_deliverable.title: The plan spine — baseline, change control, WSJF, portfolio, dependency graph and MSP rows, with the ten-scenario gate

review.findings: This retrospective Phase-G review, dated 2026-11-26, carries the level the record supports: the live Phase-G review 01a1ff8b-b3ac-7082-bc16-df2f97bd7f8d is compliant against the delivery contract 01a1ff8a-754f-70de-a63a-fa8d00596433, the scope baseline 01a1ff8a-b4f0-7e6e-9cc7-4231076e1039 is approved, and the seven Phase A–D artefacts in this pack are authored against the plan spine. The gate clauses are proved by named tests: plan_spine.rs::a_baseline_does_not_move_when_rows_change, ::a_change_request_without_impact_is_refused, ::wsjf_recomputes_when_an_input_changes, ::the_portfolio_lists_only_the_in_flight_set, ::a_two_node_dependency_cycle_is_refused, ::a_deep_dependency_cycle_leaves_no_row, ::a_benefit_without_baseline_target_method_or_owner_is_refused, ::a_benefit_map_edge_names_its_five_levels and ::a_tranche_review_without_evidence_is_refused, with approval_dual.rs::the_requester_cannot_decide_their_own_gate and programme_baseline.rs::the_taker_cannot_approve_their_own_baseline for the refused self-approval. # Project brief — T1 Plan spine (retrospective, 2026-11-26)

## Outcome

The conveyor has a plan spine: a baseline that does not move, a change request carrying an impact block and the baseline it changes, a refused self-approval, WSJF recomputed from four typed inputs with no stored score, an in-flight portfolio read, an acyclic dependency graph, and MSP rows that make a benefit a measurement record and a tranche review evidence-bearing. The build also selects the phase template, gate set and job family from the project type and enforces the Definition of Done from the card type.

## Boundary

T1 owns the rows, action families and refusals. The decision ladder is T2, the PM job is T3, cadence materialisation, PI planning and the benefits-realization procedure are T10, and metrics are T11. V1's `outline` tree is untouched and not backfilled. The Portfolio page's WSJF-backlog, cadence and capacity tabs remain fixtures, and the Plan tab's WBS, baseline and register screens are T1 work recorded here rather than a delivered console; only `portfolio.in_flight` is live.

## Reuse sources

The build reuses the existing programme and project aggregates, the approval and approval_decision rows, the one gate primitive in `crates/actions/src/control/approvals.rs` with its required-decisions rule and approver index, the programme action family's dependency assertion and its bounded `meta.depends_on` fallback, the project board actions, and the repository's real-Postgres action and API test harness. It widens `governed_asset`'s kind CHECK rather than forking a second narrative store.

## Inception units

The published inception analysis and architecture design of 2026-11-16, both measured at main, are the analysis the build starts from; the design records the decisions and the ten scenarios P1.1 to P5.3. The retrospective reconstitutes the governance record over the delivered commit `e3d7c4eb` of 2026-11-17: charter, Statement of Architecture Work, the seven A–D artefacts, the delivery contract, the WBS deliverable, the Phase-G review, this brief, the evidence page and the closure review.

## Dependencies

T1 depends on T0 and P0, recorded as `needs` edges in the project row. Its dependants are T2 and T3 and, through the specification's dependency line, T9 and T10, which read the WBS, baseline, register, dependency, tranche and benefit rows. In governance the rework depends on the standing delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14, the approved scope baseline 01a1ff8a-b4f0-7e6e-9cc7-4231076e1039 and the delivery contract 01a1ff8a-754f-70de-a63a-fa8d00596433, with the closure gate decided by an approver other than the requester.

## Acceptance

The SPEC_V2 §12 gate: one project with a baseline, a change request and a refused self-approval; WSJF recomputes from inputs; the portfolio view lists the in-flight set; a dependency cycle is refused; a benefit profile without baseline, target, method or owner is refused; a benefit-map edge names its five levels. Each clause has a named test in plan_spine.rs, approval_dual.rs or programme_baseline.rs, and `acceptance/programme/T1.toml` is the rework's acceptance instrument. The closure gate is approved by an identity distinct from the requester.

## Capabilities

Baseline and change control; dual control on every gate; WSJF prioritisation; the in-flight portfolio; the dependency graph and cycle refusal; programme-definition rows for shared configuration, tranches, cadences, stakeholder profiles and programme baselines; the benefit measurement record and five-level map; the evidence-bearing tranche review; project typing and the DoD gate. Cadence materialisation and the benefits-realization procedure are recorded as T10's, and the console surfaces beyond `portfolio.in_flight` are recorded as partial.

## Plan

The plan is `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §12, with §8.2, §8.3 and §10.3; the project row's plan pointer is `docs/SPEC_V2.md#12` and no separate plan document exists. The build landed on 2026-11-17 as commit `e3d7c4eb` for issue #72. This brief is retrospective and dated 2026-11-26: it records that build and the governance reconstituted over it, and it does not claim a contemporaneous record or a console delivery the build did not make.

# Closure review — T1 Plan spine (retrospective, 2026-11-26)

## Outcome vs acceptance

The outcome the charter records is a project plan the conveyor can be held to, and the acceptance the record carries matches it: the SPEC_V2 §12 gate is a baseline, a change request and a refused self-approval; WSJF recomputed from inputs; the in-flight portfolio; a refused dependency cycle; a refused benefit profile missing baseline, target, method or owner; and a benefit-map edge naming its five levels.
